lens: validity, feasibility and internal consistency (round 3, final pass on plan_v3.txt)

findings.title: G14 (and G8(b) as worded) fire on the main pipeline's own executor: every pick, place and post-action lift runs IK save/restore on the EXECUTING robot
findings.problem: G14 traps resetJointState on the robot on the executing client and exempts only D9's set-up, the plan-twin mirror and the IK save/restore on the PLAN-client robot (streams.py:416-418, 470-473). But execution-time IK runs on the executing client: execute_pick sets pc = env.client_id and calls solve_ik(robot_id, ..., pc) twice; execute_place and execute_stack do the same; _apply_post_action_lift calls solve_ik on the executing robot after every pick and place. solve_ik resets the executing arm to the seed, to each candidate, then restores it (and zeroes joint velocities). So every pick and place increments the G14 counter, G21 fails the episode, and B7's GO criterion (G1-G21 green) can never be met. The obvious ad hoc fix, exempting resetJointState on the executing robot, is exactly the hole that would let a CB#123-style teleport home pass, so it has to be designed now, not improvised in B7. G8(b) has the same scope defect: 'robot' is a name with no OBJECT boxel, and the executor queries getContactPoints(bodyA=robot_id) on the executing client in several places.
findings.evidence: execution.py:1058 (pc = env.client_id), :1080, :1091 (pick IK), :1380-1381 (place), :1582-1594 (stack), :868-888 (_apply_post_action_lift -> solve_ik on pc); robot_utils.py:556-567 (reset to seed), :617-619 (reset to candidate), :668-672 (restore); G8(b) robot queries: execution.py:483, :1169, :1255; robot_utils.py:468, :917; test_full_pipeline.py:283.
findings.required_change: Pre-register now either (a) a G14 exemption scoped to robot_utils.solve_ik on the executing robot's ARM joints, with the hook asserting that no stepSimulation occurs inside the call and that positions are restored to the saved values on exit (velocity zeroing disclosed in a BF#), plus the G1 allowlist entries robot_utils.py:235, 269, 324, 327, 566, 618, 671; or (b) move execution-time IK to the plan twin as a main-pipeline change under the B3 acceptance. Reword G8(b) so the robot, plane and table are outside the hidden-body rule while task bodies without an OBJECT boxel stay trapped.

findings.title: G16 makes update_object_positions raise, but main() calls it unconditionally after its own Phase-1 settle and six more times in the loop; D9's settle and die-hidden assert collide with main()'s settle
findings.plan_location: G16 (:208-210), B3(c) oracle_phases (:672-679), D9 steps (5)-(6) and the die-hidden assert (:531-540), B2 deliverable (:651-655)
findings.problem: main() runs a 50-step settle and then env.update_object_positions() at test_full_pipeline.py:562-564 before Phase 2, and calls it again at :1734, :1845, :1906, :2085, :2153 and inside every release at execution.py:623. B3(c)'s oracle_phases=False skips only the :576 check and Phase 4. With the adapter raising, B2's deliverable crashes at :564, G16's 'counters read 0' is unsatisfiable, and B7's 'no harness exception' fails. Separately, D9 places '(5) settle 50 steps (our Phase-1 settle, :562)' and '(6) the first render' inside execute_fn with the die-hidden assert between them; if execute_fn settles before calling main(), main() adds a second 50-step settle after the assert; if main()'s settle is D9's settle, the assert has to sit inside main() and no B3 keyword provides that. ObjectInfo.position is read only by spawn code and the Phase-4 oracle (boxel_env.py:1365, test_full_pipeline.py:696), so gating the calls is decision-neutral, but it is still a behaviour change that the plan does not list.
findings.required_change: B3(c): oracle_phases=False (or a separate keyword) also gates :562-564 and the in-loop update_object_positions calls, under the B3 A/A acceptance. State which component performs D9's single 50-step settle and put the die-hidden assert and the settle-displacement log between that settle and Phase 2's get_camera_observation (test_full_pipeline.py:610).

findings.title: G5 now fails the rediscovery path's removal of LATERAL fragments, which v3 leaves in place; and the discovery path does not carve against existing fragments, so M2's partition claim is false there
findings.problem: (a) The sense-discovery rediscovery cleanup deletes every id in old_obj.shadow_boxel_ids from the registry and the belief (belief.remove_shadow) with no render. v3 exempts only interior ids (separate list). G5 fails any removal without a render of that region's grid and names this very path as what it catches. Relocated cups are the expected rediscovery case in find_dice (F9 allows three per object), so arm O episodes will trip G5 and fail the gate under G21; no package changes the lateral cleanup and no G5 channel covers it. (b) On the same path new fragments are carved only against OBJECT boxels (other_solids), whereas register_new_detections carves against solids AND existing fragments. M2 says interiors are carved 'as lateral fragments are, so the at-most-one-SHADOW-per-point invariant (audit #68) holds'; on the discovery path neither lateral fragments nor an interior cast at a rediscovery are carved against existing fragments, so an interior can overlap an existing interior or lateral fragment.
findings.evidence: execution.py:2871-2884 (unrendered removal incl. belief.remove_shadow), :2960-2980 (other_solids = OBJECT boxels only), :2278-2279 (register_new_detections carves against existing fragments); plan_v3.txt:113-123, :448-453, :814-821; round-2 log N12 took only option (1) of verify_r2_pod's required change.
findings.required_change: Decide before B5: either the cleanup keeps every superseded lateral fragment that does not render empty (as retire_lost_objects does), as a main-pipeline change with its BF# and the B3 acceptance, or G5 gains an enumerated 'superseded by recast' channel and P4.5 CORRECTIONS discloses that unknown fragments are dropped unobserved on rediscovery. B5 states one carve set for every registration path: all OBJECT boxels except the caster plus all existing SHADOW fragments, interiors included.

findings.title: D7's corrective path and home_not_reached bound cannot occur as specified, and D7's init list omits (Config q_home)
findings.problem: (1) For holding goals main() ends the outer loop as soon as the held body is the target (_loop_done), so after a failed at-home test no replan happens and the 'two consecutive planned moves to q_home' bound never fires. (2) If the loop did replan, the corrective move cannot be planned: the readback config is built like :1594 (joints and name only), and streams.home_config carries no ignored or held ids, so plan_motion neither ignores nor tracks the held die; sync_to_plan_client puts the held body at the end effector and is_config_collision_free rejects any robot contact with a non-ignored body, so the start configuration is in collision and main() falls through to the goal-(handempty) disposal plan, which puts the die down. The nominal path works only because q1 is the compute-kin config carrying ignored={die}. (3) D7 lists '(Boxel home) (config_for_boxel q_home home)' but not (Config q_home); init emits Config only for current_config, and move needs (Config ?q2); B4 does list (Config q_clear), so the two sections disagree. (4) home_config's joints are REST_POSES, not their DEFAULT_ARM_POS, and B3 lists no parameter for them, for the goal form or for the loop termination.
findings.evidence: test_full_pipeline.py:1201-1209 (_loop_done), :1591-1597, :1375-1399 (disposal plan); streams.py:255-258 (home_config = REST_POSES, name q_home), :918-937 (held inference from endpoint metadata); boxel_env.py:748-749; robot_utils.py:74, :274-304; pddlstream_planner.py:889-890; domain_pddlstream.pddl:207-216; tampura_environments panda_utils/robot.py:36-44.
findings.required_change: B3(d) lists explicitly: a goal override; loop termination = the goal test including D7's at-home evaluator; home_config joints from task_spec (DEFAULT_ARM_POS); (Config q_home) emitted in init; the post-pick config and every q_readback_k carry the held die's held_body_ids, ignored_body_ids and grasp_ee_offset. Add a B3 or B7 test in which a corrective move to q_home is planned while holding.

findings.title: D12's primary interpreter cannot import tampura, and its history pickle fails G6; the fallback puts our dependencies into arm T's venv
findings.problem: (a) Arm O needs Policy, TampuraEnv and structs, so it imports tampura; tampura/__init__.py imports tampura.policies, whose __init__ imports dqn_policy, which imports torch, gymnasium, stable_baselines3 and torch.utils.tensorboard. wsl_env has none of these (and none of trimesh, scipy, imageio, yaml); D12 pins only trimesh, scipy, imageio and adds pyyaml. Adding torch and stable_baselines3 to wsl_env may also move its numpy 2.2.6, the configuration our pipeline is validated in and the B3 A/A baseline. (b) G6 requires the RolloutHistory pickle to load in their venv (numpy 1.24.4); a history written under numpy 2.x references numpy._core, which numpy 1.24 lacks, so G6 is expected to be red by construction on D12's primary path. (c) The fallback, 'arm O runs in their venv', means installing our dependencies into arm T's environment, which G13 does not guard (it hashes only the git trees), and running the c31cbdd A/A under numpy 1.24, which is untested.
findings.evidence: tampura/__init__.py:1-3; tampura/policies/__init__.py:4; tampura/policies/dqn_policy.py:11-16; wsl_env/lib/python3.10/site-packages has no torch, gymnasium, stable_baselines3, tensorboard, trimesh, scipy, imageio or yaml (checked); plan_v3.txt:131-132, :339-341, :568-577.
findings.required_change: B1(j) parity also covers 'import tampura' and the full import set of their packages, a G6 pickle round trip into their venv, and a smoke run of our holding scene. Arm O gets its own venv (a clone of theirs plus our dependencies, or wsl_env plus their full import set), never their venv. campaign.json records a pip-freeze hash for both environments, and G13 asserts that arm T's freeze is unchanged before and after every run.

findings.title: Packages are labelled 'dependency order' but B2 and B1 depend on later packages
findings.problem: B2's deliverable 'builds OBJECT, lateral and INTERIOR boxels' needs M2, which is B5; it also needs W and the D8 class constants (octree auto_cell from the largest declared class), which are frozen in B6, and B3(a) RobotModel, B3(b) adopt-client constructor and B3(c) main(env), all scheduled after B2. B1, 'read-only reconnaissance' due 2026-11-02, needs B3 code too: (f) and (h) need our IK on their Panda by link name (B3(a)); (i) measures 'under the D7 final hold', which B3(d) implements; (e) needs our detector rendering through the D4 camera. B2 also says the plan twin is built 'through the existing _mirror_* helpers', but _mirror_load_urdf loads into BOTH clients, which would add a second Panda to their executing world, and _mirror_spawn_object builds only primitives, not YCB meshes.
findings.required_change: Reorder: B3(a)(b)(c) before B2. B2's deliverable is OBJECT and lateral boxels; interiors move to B5. B2 uses B1's measured W as provisional values, frozen in B6. B1(e)(f)(h)(i) either run on declared probe code whose result B3 must reproduce, or move after B3. B3(b) adds plan-client-only mirror variants and asserts that the executing client's body count is unchanged.

findings.title: The review-gate list disagrees between P4.1 and B7, and the domain tweak M1 (B4) is never reviewed
findings.problem: P4.1 runs the adversarial review on the diffs of B2+B3, B5 and B7 and on the B8 report, each before the next package starts. B7 says 'The agent review of the B2+B3+B5+B6 diffs runs here', which moves the B2+B3 review to after B4-B6 and adds B6. The calendar budgets four gates. Under either list, B4, the only change to the planner's domain (M1), gets no adversarial review, and under P4.1 neither do B6's constants or M6.
findings.required_change: One list, stated once: B2+B3 before B4; B4+B5+B6 (every model tweak and the frozen constants) before B7; B7 before B8; the B8 report. Recount the gates in the calendar.

findings.title: P4.6 does not say what a gate-failed episode is, and its machine rules do not cover the runs that feed pre-registered decisions
findings.problem: (a) G21 makes any hook count 'fail the episode's gate check', but neither P4.6 nor B8 says whether such an episode counts as a failure for its arm, is excluded, or aborts the campaign. Exclusion would be a dropped seed, which P4.6 forbids, and choosing after seeing which arm and seed tripped is a post hoc degree of freedom. Given the first three findings, gate trips are likely. (b) MACHINE (idle machine, CB#113 paused, pgrep) binds only B8. B1(g), arm T's reproduction reference whose per-seed outcomes drive the agreement rule, and the B3, B5 and M6 A/A and A/B acceptances, whose wall-clock noise floor decides pass or fail, have no machine rule, while CB#113 is a live sweep. (c) The pgrep patterns 'test_full_pipeline' and 'run_planner' match none of the campaign drivers (run_bridge_on_finddice.py, run_tampura_timed.py, tampura_sweep.py), and D10 attributes the 900 s kill to tampura_sweep.py while B8 runs T through _bridge_campaign.py.
findings.required_change: Pre-register: in B8 a gate-failed episode counts as a failure for its arm, keeps its row and is flagged with the hook name; a gate trip in B7 blocks GO. Apply MACHINE to B1(g) and to every acceptance run. Give pgrep patterns for all four drivers, and name _bridge_campaign.py as the owner of the 900 s cap on both arms.

findings.title: Calendar arithmetic and window disagree with the listed efforts and milestones
findings.problem: The listed efforts (B0 3, B1 2-3, B2 5-7, B3 4-5, B4 1-2, B5 3-4, B6 1-2 or up to 4 with M6, B7 3, B8 4) sum to 26-33 agent-days, or 26-35 with M6, not '27 to 34'. With about 3 review days that is 29-38, so the high end exceeds the 35-day window. The window is stated to end 2026-11-30, but the B8 milestone is 2026-12-02.
findings.required_change: Correct the sums, state the M6 case separately, and align the window end with the B8 milestone (or the milestone with the window).
